items.zones: Alaska and Hawaii-Aleutian (western Aleutians); zones from geography, not quoted from an official page
items.hours_quote: General Election Day – Polling Places are open from 7am to 8pm.
items.tracker_quote: The Voter Information Tool can check registration, application, and ballot status.
items.notes: Hours from the Division of Elections 2026 General Election media packet (Nov 3 entry). Polling place page also says "Polling Places are open from 7:00am to 8:00pm." (pages4/AK_polls.txt). The 2026 absentee application (pages4/AK_C06A.txt) also points to myvoterportal.alaska.gov; older forms used myvoterinformation.alaska.gov. No official in-line sentence found.

items.zones: Central; the 2026 Voter Guide says polling places in the Eastern Time Zone may be open 7 A.M. to 7 P.M. Eastern Time
items.line_rule: Anyone who attempts to join the voting line after 7:00 P.M. shall not be permitted to vote.
items.hours_quote: On Election Day, polls will be open 7 am to 7 pm.
items.tracker_quote: Track the status of your absentee ballot.
items.notes: SOS press release for the November 3, 2026 General Election. Eastern-zone quote: "Please note that polling places located in the Eastern Time Zone may be open from 7 A.M. to 7 P.M. Eastern Time." (pages4/AL_voterguide.txt, 2026 Voter Guide). Line rule is from the same Voter Guide. Tracker link text on sos.alabama.gov absentee page points to myinfo.alabamavotes.gov/voterview.

items.line_rule: Allow any voters already in line at 7:30 p.m. to vote
items.hours_quote: November 3, 2026 General Election Day - Polls open 7:30 am to 7:30 pm
items.tracker_quote: Confirm your address, party association, ballot statuses, and polling place locations.
items.notes: Hours source is the State Board of Election Commissioners 2026 Election Coordinator Manual (sbec.arkansas.gov). SOS voting page also says "Vote at your poll on Election Day from 7:30 a.m. to 7:30 p.m." (pages4/AR_votingin.txt). Line rule is a poll-worker instruction in the same manual. SOS absentee page links VoterView (voterview.ar-nova.org, a state-linked SOS tool).

items.line_rule: Any qualified voter who at the moment of closing is in the line of waiting voters shall be allowed to vote.
items.hours_quote: For any election called pursuant to the laws of this state, the polls shall be opened in every precinct at 6:00 a.m. on the day of election and shall be closed at 7:00 p.m.
items.tracker_quote: You may track the status of your ballot at (link is external)my.arizona.vote to confirm that it was received and counted.
items.notes: Statute A.R.S. 16-565. azsos.gov pages return 403 to curl; early-voting page read in Chrome. The same page says Pima and Maricopa voters should check with their county for status updates. Arizona does not observe DST; the Navajo Nation does (lead only, not checked against an official source).

items.hours_quote: Polling locations are established by county elections officials and are open from 7:00 a.m. to 8:00 p.m. on Election Day, Tuesday, November 3, 2026.
items.tracker_quote: Sign-up at WheresMyBallot.sos.ca.gov to receive automatic email, SMS (text), or voice call notifications about your ballot.
items.notes: Key Dates page also says "Election Day - Polls shall be open throughout the state from 7:00 a.m. to 8:00 p.m." (pages4/CA_keydates.txt). WheresMyBallot link on the SOS page resolves to california.ballottrax.net/voter/. No in-line sentence on the saved SOS pages; Elections Code 14401 page blocked (403).

items.line_rule: Voters must submit their ballot or be in line to vote by 7:00 PM for their ballot to be counted.
items.hours_quote: In-person voting on Election Day, Tuesday, November 3, will be available from 7:00 AM - 7:00 PM.
items.tracker_quote: Colorado voters in all 64 counties can track their ballot for the 2026 General Election using BallotTrax, a program that was implemented statewide by Secretary of State Jena Griswold in 2020.
items.notes: All-mail state; hours are for in-person voting at voter service and polling centers (SOS release Oct 19, 2026). Tracker from SOS release Sep 15, 2026; link "State of Colorado BallotTrax". Denver historically used its own BallotTrace (lead only).

items.line_rule: No elector shall be permitted to cast such elector's vote after the hour prescribed for the closing of the polls in any election unless such elector is in line at eight o'clock p.m.
items.hours_quote: the polls on the day of such election shall remain open for voting from six o'clock a.m. until eight o'clock p.m.
items.tracker_quote: If you have returned your completed absentee ballot to your municipal clerk, you can check the status of the ballot here.
items.notes: C.G.S. 9-174 (chapter 146). The 2026 SOTS voter guide also lists "6 a.m. − 8 p.m.: Polls Open" (pages4/CT_guide2026.txt). Tracker sentence is on the SOTS military and overseas voters page; "here" links to the Voter Registration Lookup. It shows return status only, not mailing.

items.hours_quote: Election Day Vote Centers are open from 7:00 A.M. to 8:00 P.M.
items.tracker_quote: Track Your Ballot
items.notes: DCBOE "Time Off to Vote 2026 General" notice (Election Day Tuesday, November 3, 2026). Vote centers, any center citywide. Tracker is the "Track Your Ballot" link on dcboe.org (BallotTrax). No official in-line sentence found.

items.line_rule: permit those electors to vote who have presented themselves and have offered to vote prior to 8:00 p.m., provided that at 8:00 p.m. they shall be in a line awaiting their turn to vote
items.hours_quote: Polling Places are open from 7 a.m. until 8 p.m. on General Election Day, November 3, 2026.
items.tracker_quote: Check the status using Delaware's online voter portal;
items.notes: Line rule from 15 Del. C. ch. 49 subch. II (statute). Statute also says the general election opens "at 7:00 in the morning". Tracker: DE absentee FAQ links "Delaware's online voter portal" to ivote.de.gov.

items.line_rule: Any voter who is standing in line at 7 p.m. (local time) in their county is still eligible to cast a vote.
items.hours_quote: Polls on Election Day are open from 7 a.m. until 7 p.m. (local time). Florida has two time-zones – Central and Eastern.
items.tracker_quote: To request a vote-by-mail ballot or to track the status of your request and/or ballot, select your county below for the direct link:
items.notes: Hours confirmed (DOS FAQ; also F.S. 100.011 in pages4/FL_100011.txt). Tracker is partial: Florida has no single state tracker; the DOS page is a state directory linking each county Supervisor of Elections tool.

items.line_rule: If you are in line by 7:00 p.m., you are allowed to cast your ballot.
items.hours_quote: Polling places are open on Election Day from 7:00 a.m. to 7:00 p.m.
items.tracker_quote: You can track your absentee ballot on your My Voter Page.
items.notes: Source is georgia.gov (state portal), "Vote in Person on Election Day", last updated June 2026. sos.ga.gov returns 403 to curl and was not in the Wayback Machine for this path. Tracker sentence from georgia.gov event page for Oct 23, 2026 (last day to request absentee ballots for the general election).

items.line_rule: If, at the closing hour of voting, any voter is standing in line at a voter service center with the desire of entering and voting, but due to the voter service center being overcrowded has been unable to do so, the voter shall be allowed to vote.
items.hours_quote: (2) On an election day, from 7:00 a.m. until the closing hour of voting.
items.tracker_quote: Additionally, you may sign up with BallotTrax to receive ballot notifications.
items.notes: All-mail state; in-person voting at voter service centers only. HRS 11-131 read via Wayback (capitol.hawaii.gov 403 to curl, Cloudflare check in Chrome); saved file URL is the web.archive.org copy. Closing hour: "Ballots must be received by the County Elections Division by close of voting, 7:00 p.m." (pages4/HI_voting.txt). Tracker: elections.hawaii.gov links BallotTrax; Aug 2026 newsletter says "Track Your Ballot: Sign up for ballot tracking alerts at elections.hawaii.gov." (pages4/HI_news826.txt).

items.hours_quote: At all elections, except as otherwise permitted by this section, the polls shall be opened at 7:00 a.m.
items.tracker_quote: You can track your absentee ballot online by using the Track Your Absentee Ballot search.
items.notes: Iowa Code 2026, section 49.73. Closing: "The polling places shall be closed at 8:00 p.m. for all elections." (same file). The noon-opening exception applies only to benefited-district and unincorporated-area elections. sos.iowa.gov returns 403 to curl; FAQ read in Chrome. The FAQ body link uses sos.iowa.gov/elections/absenteeballotstatus/absentee/search; the site header uses the apps. host. No in-line sentence found.

items.zones: Mountain and Pacific (northern Idaho); zones from geography, not quoted
items.varies_note: The county clerk, at his option, however, may open the polls in his county at 7:00 A.M. for a primary or general election.
items.line_rule: Any elector who is in line at 8:00 P.M. shall be allowed to vote notwithstanding the pronouncement that the polls are closed.
items.hours_quote: Vote in person on Election Day, November 3. Polling locations are open from 8:00 a.m. – 8:00 p.m.
items.tracker_quote: Check The Status Of Your Absentee Ballot On Your Voter Record.
items.notes: VoteIdaho 2026 General Election page. varies_note and line rule quoted from Idaho Code 34-1101 (pages4/ID_34-1101.txt). Tracker link is the "Absentee Ballot Status" button on voteidaho.gov/casting-your-ballot.

items.hours_quote: The polls shall be opened at the hour of 6:00 a.m. and continued open until 7:00 p.m. of the same day
items.tracker_quote: If you wish to check the status of your vote by mail ballot, you will need to contact your election authority.
items.notes: 10 ILCS 5/17-1. No statewide tracker: the State Board says some local election authorities offer tracking on their own sites. No in-line sentence found in the saved sources.

items.zones: Eastern and Central; zones from geography, not quoted (official sources say "prevailing local time")
items.hours_quote: Polls are open 6:00 a.m. to 6:00 p.m., prevailing local time.
items.tracker_quote: GET ABSENTEE BALLOT INFORMATION
items.notes: Hours confirmed: Election Division 2026 Calendar Brochure (General Election Day entry); 2026 Election Day Handbook also says "The polls must remain open continuously from 6:00 a.m. to 6:00 p.m. prevailing local time." (pages4/IN_edhandbook.txt). Tracker partial: the portal has a "GET ABSENTEE BALLOT INFORMATION" menu item, but no saved official sentence says it shows ballot status. No in-line sentence found.

items.hours: 7 a.m. to 7 p.m. (counties may open as early as 6 a.m. and close as late as 8 p.m.)
items.zones: Central and Mountain (four western counties); zones from geography, not quoted
items.varies_note: State law allow counties to open polling locations as early as 6:00 a.m. and close as late as 8:00 p.m.
items.hours_quote: State law requires polling places to open at 7:00 a.m. and close at 7:00 p.m. on election day.
items.tracker_quote: Advance Mail Ballot Tracker
items.notes: SOS voter information page (cites K.S.A. 25-106, 12 consecutive hours minimum). Tracker: July 27, 2026 SOS release lists "Advance Mail Ballot Tracker" among VoterView features and links VoterView at kansasvoterinfo.gov; it tells media to use votekansas.gov. No in-line sentence found.

items.zones: Eastern and Central; zones from geography, not quoted ("local time")
items.line_rule: If you are in line at 6:00 PM, you will be allowed to vote.
items.hours_quote: Polls are open from 6:00 AM to 6:00 PM local time on Tuesday, November 3rd, 2026.
items.tracker_quote: And, check the status of your requested absentee ballot
items.notes: State Board of Elections FAQ. The page text has zero-width characters after "3rd"; quote check strips them. Tracker read in Chrome (403 to curl).

items.line_rule: All voters in line at 8 p.m. have the right to vote.
items.hours_quote: On election day, the polls are open from 6 a.m.-8 p.m.
items.tracker_quote: You can track the status of your absentee ballot here.
items.notes: SURPRISE: 6 a.m., not the usual 7 a.m. The SOS Election Dates entry for the Tuesday, November 3, 2026 "U.S. Senate General/Open U.S. Representative Primary/Open Primary Election" gives 6 a.m.-8 p.m. This matches R.S. 18:541(B) (6 a.m. for regularly scheduled congressional primary elections and elections held at the same time) and the Ways to Vote page ("6 a.m. for TUESDAY elections"). The "here" link on Ways to Vote has a broken href (voterportal.--environment--.sos.la.gov); the Louisiana Voter Portal is the intended tool.

items.hours: 7 a.m. to 8 p.m. (some towns open as early as 5:45 a.m.)
items.varies_note: Your city or town may choose to open the polls as early as 5:45 a.m. Check with your local election office to find out if your community opens before 7 a.m. on Election Day.
items.hours_quote: For state elections, state primaries, and presidential primaries, all polling places will be open on Election Day from 7 a.m. until 8 p.m.
items.tracker_quote: Use our Track My Ballot tool to check the status of your ballot.
items.notes: Secretary of the Commonwealth pages read in Chrome (curl gets JS stub). The statute (M.G.L. c.54 s.64, pages4/MA_c54s64.txt) allows opening from 5:45 a.m. to 7 a.m. The polling hours page says "all polling places will be open ... from 7 a.m."; a 2026 Uniform Polling Hours cost-certification FAQ exists on mass.gov (403, not read), so check whether early openings still apply. No in-line sentence found.

items.line_rule: (b) A voter who has appeared at a polling place by the closing hour to cast a ballot shall be allowed to vote.
items.hours_quote: (a) On an election day, a polling place shall be open from 7 a.m. until 8 p.m.
items.tracker_quote: Visit the voter look-up website to verify if your local board of elections received your request for a ballot and the status of your mail-in ballot.
items.notes: Md. Code, Election Law 10-301 (mgaleg.maryland.gov).

items.hours: Opens between 6 a.m. and 8 a.m. (10 a.m. in towns under 500), closes 8 p.m.
items.varies_note: The municipal officers of each municipality shall determine the time of opening the polls within these limits.
items.hours_quote: The polls must be opened no earlier than 6 a.m. and no later than 8 a.m. on election day, except that in municipalities with a population of less than 500, the polls must be opened no later than 10:00 a.m.
items.tracker_quote: Already requested your absentee ballot? You can track your request online!
items.notes: 21-A M.R.S. 626. Closing: "The polls must be closed at 8 p.m. on election day, except in municipalities of population less than 100 which may close the polls after all registered voters have voted." (same file). No in-line sentence found.

items.zones: Eastern and Central (four western Upper Peninsula counties); zones from geography, not quoted
items.line_rule: Every qualified elector present and in line at the polls at the hour prescribed for the closing thereof shall be allowed to vote.
items.hours_quote: On the day of any election, the polls shall be opened at 7 o'clock in the forenoon, and shall be continuously open until 8 o'clock in the afternoon and no longer.
items.tracker_quote: Voters can securely track the mailing and receipt of their absentee ballot application and absentee ballot at Michigan.gov/Vote.
items.notes: MCL 168.720. Tracker link "Track the status of your absentee ballot" on michigan.gov/sos absentee page points to mvic.sos.state.mi.us.

items.hours: 7 a.m. to 8 p.m. (some small towns may start later, up to 10 a.m.)
items.varies_note: The later time may not be later than 10:00 a.m. for special, primary, or general elections.
items.line_rule: Voting must not be allowed after the time when it is scheduled to end, unless individuals are waiting in the polling place or waiting in line at the door to register, to update the voter's registration, or to vote.
items.hours_quote: Except as otherwise provided in this section, at the state primary and the state general election the hours for voting in every precinct in the state shall begin at 7:00 a.m. and shall extend continuously until 8:00 p.m.
items.tracker_quote: Use the Track your ballot tool to find out when election officials received your ballot.
items.notes: Minn. Stat. 204C.05 (towns under 500 outside the metro area may vote at town meeting for later start; unorganized territories by petition). SOS site moved to sos.mn.gov; old sos.state.mn.us paths 404. Vote-by-mail page read in Chrome; its Track your ballot link redirects to mnvotes.sos.mn.gov/abstatus/index.

items.line_rule: However, those individuals in line at 7:00 p.m. will be allowed to vote.
items.hours_quote: Polling places open at 6:00 a.m. and remain open until 7:00 p.m.
items.notes: Hours confirmed (SOS Election Day FAQ; How to Vote page also says "POLLING PLACES ARE OPEN FROM 6:00 AM TO 7:00 PM ON ELECTION DAY." in pages4/MO_vote.txt). Tracker not_found: no statewide absentee ballot tracker for domestic voters found on sos.mo.gov; search leads point only to the Military and Overseas Voting Access Portal. Check with the local election authority.

items.line_rule: Any voter in line at 7:00 p.m. is legally entitled to cast a ballot.
items.hours_quote: Polls will open at 7:00 a.m. and close at 7:00 p.m.
items.tracker_quote: Mississippians who have requested an absentee ballot may track their ballot utilizing the My Election Day portal.
items.notes: Hours partial: quote is from the SOS March 3, 2026 release for the March 10, 2026 primary; no Nov 2026 Election Day reminder found yet. The Oct 19, 2026 general-election absentee report says "County election officials can tabulate ballots at the closing of the polls on Election Day (7 p.m.)." (pages4/MS_absrep.txt), supporting the 7 p.m. close. Statute (Miss. Code 23-15-541) not available on an official free site. Tracker confirmed.

items.hours: 7 a.m. to 8 p.m. (polling places with fewer than 400 voters may open at noon)
items.varies_note: (2) (a) A polling place having fewer than 400 registered electors who intend to vote at the polling place must be open from at least noon to 8 p.m. or until all registered electors in any precinct have voted, at which time that precinct in the polling place must be closed immediately.
items.hours_quote: (1) Except as provided in subsections (2)(a) and (3), polling places must be open from 7 a.m. to 8 p.m.
items.tracker_quote: Montana’s absentee voters can use VoteMT.gov to track the status of their absentee ballot from the time it is sent to when it is received and accepted by their local election office.
items.notes: MCA 13-1-106 (archive.legmt.gov copy of current code). sosmt.gov returns 403 to curl; SOS release (June 2026 primary) read in Chrome. No in-line sentence found.
